startup.name: Luel
startup.one_liner: Turning everyday words and actions into usable training data.
startup.description: Luel is a sourcing and licensing platform for rights-cleared multimodal training data at scale. We work with frontier AI teams to provide high-quality bespoke data collections and off-the-shelf datasets.

yc_acceptance.basis: Roughly 1 percent base rate. Conditional on acceptance this is a note: a twelve person team selling to frontier AI labs and a category YC favored, so the estimate sits above the base.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly worry that data sourcing is a services marketplace with concentrated buyers, thin margins and copyright exposure, and that frontier labs build data pipelines in house. The estimate leans on the cohort base rates in stage_benchmarks.md, where later rounds are rare and slow, and on what happened to comparable YC companies such as sieve and panels.

anchors.adjustment_reason: Above the 59 percent recent anchor but near the 81 percent older anchor. AI data infrastructure with twelve people and buyers among frontier labs was among the fastest funded categories in early 2026.

ladder.why_it_fails: The seed most plausibly fails because revenue is lumpy and concentrated in a few buyers. Panels, a YC audio data company, and Sieve, a multimodal data lab, show the category is crowded and that only some raise seeds. Investors may also worry about the legal risk behind rights clearance and about Scale AI, Mercor and Surge competing on data services.

outcomes.why_it_fails: A stall is likely because few buyers control demand and prices. Data labeling incumbents are larger, and legal risk over rights clearance can erase value. Exits are most likely sales to larger data firms, though a rare outcome above 1B is possible if it becomes a licensing exchange.

killers.risk: Frontier labs build data pipelines in house
killers.evidence: Labs have large budgets and have acquired or built data teams, so demand for outside sourcing can shift.
killers.mitigation: Specialize in modalities and rights that labs cannot easily source.

killers.evidence: A handful of labs pay for bespoke collections, and contracts are project based.
killers.mitigation: Convert projects into off the shelf dataset licenses.

killers.evidence: Licensing data has legal exposure if rights are not truly cleared, as ongoing AI copyright disputes show.
killers.mitigation: Document consent chains and use insurance.

killers.risk: Scale AI, Mercor and Surge compete
killers.evidence: Large vendors already serve labs with deep budgets. This is visible in the comparable YC companies and the competitor sources listed in this evaluation.

competition_now.name: Scale AI
competition_now.what: Data labeling and collection for labs.
competition_now.traction: Market leader with large lab contracts.

competition_now.name: Veritone and Troveo
competition_now.what: Rights cleared video and audio data marketplaces.
competition_now.traction: Troveo says access to training material is now a bigger constraint than labeling.

technical_complexity.rationale: Collecting multimodal data at scale and clearing rights is operationally hard: contracts, quality checks, consent and storage. A small team can run the first collections, but a durable supply side takes capital.

takeover_risk.rationale: Incumbents have the relationships, but exclusive supply is slow to copy. The timeline is an estimate for a well resourced rival with existing distribution and an incentive to copy the idea.

evidence.claim: The AI training dataset market is estimated around 8.7B dollars in 2025 growing about 33 percent a year by one research firm.
Licensing data is becoming a bigger constraint than labeling for developers, per a data platform.

actions: Build an off the shelf catalog.
roadmap.proof: Repeat revenue from the same buyers.
Annualized revenue above 5M and under 70 percent concentration.

pros.point: Twelve person team in a hot AI infrastructure category.
pros.evidence: Team size in the input and a market growing fast.
Frontier labs pay large sums for data.

pros.point: Rights cleared data answers a real legal need.
pros.evidence: Developers cite access to cleared content as a constraint.

brand.name: Luel
brand.name_check: python3 -I scripts/name_features.py --score "Luel" --era 2022+ : one word invented name, four characters, one syllable.
strengths: Short and invented, easy to trademark.
brand.rationale: Short invented one word names are common among strong recent YC brands and are easy to own, though the name carries no meaning. Effect on success is small.

narrative.headline: A well timed AI data supplier likely to raise a seed fast, with real risk from buyer concentration and in house pipelines.
narrative.general_summary: Luel sells rights cleared multimodal training data to frontier AI teams. Demand is strong and a team of twelve is large for a winter 2026 startup. The likeliest path is a quick seed, then a harder Series A where buyers and prices are tested. Scale AI, Mercor and other vendors are bigger. The comparable YC data companies mostly have no later rounds yet, so the base rate evidence is thin. The step odds are anchored on the 2022 to 2025 B2B cohorts and the older 2018 to 2021 cohort, which differ a lot, so treat the later rounds as wide ranges.

assumptions: Founder backgrounds and customers were not provided.
Market size figures come from research firms with differing scopes.
